topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its learning objectives concerning cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional Treatment Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional approaches to cancer management—including surgical resection, radiation, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the problems of non-specific systemic toxicity and efflux pump-mediated resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Cellular Dependencies, Checkpoint Deficiencies, and DNA Repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies designed to exploit inherent molecular vulnerabilities in cancer cells, including hormone dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction, Kinase Inhibitors, and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how hyperactivated oncogenic kinases are targeted by small-molecule inhibitors and detail the molecular and pathway bypass mechanisms through which tumor cells develop drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover targeted therapeutic strategies that utilize monoclonal antibodies to directly neutralize cell-surface receptors, recruit immune effector functions, or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Tumor Immunology and Immunotherapeutic Strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between the immune system and cancer alongside therapeutic interventions that reactivate or engineer immune cells to eliminate tumors.

topics.label: Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Directions in Cancer Treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer therapy by examining historical survival trends, persistent clinical challenges like heterogeneity, and future directions in early detection and trial design.
